### Historical audit — H0179

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane3/codex_parallel_12_lane3_B_r2/infer_logs/kea-atomic-signal-selectors/turn_1/trajs.json`. Event citations below refer to this file; inventory figures are supplied metadata, not independently inspected evaluation files.

| Question | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The original task prompt is not visible. From the student’s reproduction and final report, the **inferred** goal was atomic selector invalidation and a selector health API, with implementation, build verification and a commit (main_agent events 34–36). This is not a complete specification. |
| Exploration and changes | The student independently inspected selector creation, context, lifecycle, React hooks, reducers and types (events 8–18, 20–28). It created branch `atomic-signal-selectors` from `master` (events 13, 19); branch status was clean in event 29. It reported no source changes or commit (event 36); inventory records a zero-byte patch. |
| Validation | An initial reproduction failed because `@babel/register` was unavailable (events 30–31). A later Babel-based run showed `selectorHealth` undefined and the name selector’s evaluation count rising from 1 to 2 after an age-only change (events 34–35). The existing selector suite passed 7/7 (events 32–33); that baseline does not validate the requested feature. |
| Teacher input | Shared hint files and an actual-system-prompt path are listed in inventory, but their contents and any delivered teacher event are not shown. **Receipt and adoption are unestablished**; availability is not evidence of either. |
| Outcome | **Empty patch, formally not solved:** supplied inventory records fail-to-pass 0/12 and pass-to-pass 139/139. The student explicitly reported implementation, build verification and commit incomplete (event 36). The run’s `success`/`end_turn` metadata describes termination, not task success (top_level_metadata, characters [0,2704)). The missing module was a local technical obstacle, not evidence that the whole session was interrupted; the later reproduction ran. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** The transferable observation is that a focused behavioral reproduction can expose a gap even when existing regression tests pass; it is not a substitute for an implementation and feature tests. The age/name invalidation and missing health method are specific to this task. Why the student stopped without implementing is unknown, as are the full requirements and any teacher influence. No attempted algorithm was submitted, so its correctness or failure cannot be assessed.
